sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Global Payroll and Staff Compliance Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate or tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition, heavily influenced by French and Belgian doctrine; unitary national system with no sub-national corporate law or tax differentiation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-Hong Kong SAR Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (signed 11 November 2018)
Luxembourg-UAE Investment Protection Agreement (1998, as supplemented)
Luxembourg-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 26 April 2019, pending entry into force)
EU-Singapore Investment Protection Agreement (IPA, in force 2023)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied since 21 September 2017)
Luxembourg-United States Income and Capital Tax Treaty (1962, as amended by 1996, 2004 and 2009 Protocols)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended), Article 15-1 (SCSp regime inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013; SCSp has no legal personality, is managed by an unlimited-liability general partner, and has no minimum capital requirement); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended) (AML/CFT Law), Articles 2-1, 4 and 5-6; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended to comply with CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 (as amended) on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 11 January 2019 on the operation of the RBE; Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds (payment rails: SEPA Direct Debit and SWIFT wire).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal — RBE access is limited to Luxembourg competent authorities, financial and non-financial obliged entities performing statutory customer due diligence, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; public access was invalidated by CJEU C-37/20 and C-601/20 (22 November 2022). Nominee arrangements are not recognized to circumvent disclosure.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and each natural-person general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent administrative authority of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) if the country of issue is a Contracting State; otherwise consular legalization by the Luxembourg consulate having competence over the issuing authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / official registration extract of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the corporate general partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization in accordance with the issuing country's status under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / certificate of non-dissolution of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or governmental agency of the corporate general partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization; must be addressed to the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and the appointing notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / register of directors and shareholders of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate secretarial provider of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of issue followed by Hague Apostille; consular legalization if the jurisdiction is not an Apostille Contracting State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill or bank statement, not older than three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated credit institution of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified notarial copy of the original document; Hague Apostille or consular legalization required at the notary's discretion for non-EEA issuers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Organizational chart and UBO structural diagram signed by the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate general partner or its Luxembourg legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal attestation signed in Luxembourg; no apostille required, but must be certified by Luxembourg counsel as accurate against underlying registry evidence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / banker's good-conduct certificate for the corporate general partner or any major limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualifying credit institution at the head office or branch of the general partner / limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original on bank letterhead signed by an authorized officer; apostille not customary for EEA banks, but consular legalization may be imposed by the notary or the onboarding Luxembourg bank for non-EEA issuers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-execution and rolling screening (minimum annually and within 24 hours of any ownership change) of all UBOs, general partners, limited partners, authorized signatories and beneficial-equivalent controllers against: (i) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions list (EU CFSP implementing EU Regulations); (ii) UN Security Council consolidated list and EU autonomous sanctions implementing UN resolutions; (iii) OFAC SDN and Capta lists (required for USD-denominated SWIFT wire rails); (iv) Luxembourg Ministry of Finance national asset-freezing list; (v) EU restrictive measures against Russia and Belarus (Regulations (EU) 269/2014 and 833/2014, as amended); and (vi) FATF high-risk jurisdiction monitoring lists. PEP status is determined under Article 4(7) of the AML/CFT Law, including immediate family members and known close associates of prominent public functionaries; enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, is mandatory for PEPs and for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier applicable to this payroll SaaS platform. Any positive hit or suspicion triggers an internal escalation to the AML/CFT compliance officer and, where warranted, a suspicious transaction report to the Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) under Articles 5-6 of the AML/CFT Law.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_obligation: Under the RBE Law, the SCSp must file its beneficial owner particulars within one month of commercial registration with the RCS; the RBE filing is a condition precedent to the notary's attestation of good standing and to full corporate effect.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.sc_sp_specific_aml_note: The SCSp has no legal personality and no minimum capital; therefore AML/CFT due diligence is performed on the general partner (and, where the GP is a corporate entity, on its directors, shareholders and ultimate natural-person controllers) and on every limited partner whose economic interest reaches or exceeds the 25% threshold or who exercises de facto control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible at www.lbr.lu with electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin characters; there is no mandatory Luxembourgish, French or German formulation for an SCSp, but the name must end with the abbreviation 'SCSp' or the full wording 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'. The name must be distinctive from all existing RCS entries and from registered trademarks; it must not mislead the public as to the legal form, activity or solvency of the entity. Names of a sole-associate SCSp must, where relevant, reflect the sole-associate character in the deed even if not in the name itself.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking — requires CSSF authorization and a regulated banking legal form
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance — requires Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA) authorization
Fonds / Fund / SICAV / SICAF / FCP — regulated fund tokens, prior CSSF or ministerial approval required
État / State / Gouvernement / Administration / Ministère / Commune — implies public authority, prior ministerial consent required
Chambre de Commerce / Chambre des Métiers — reserved statutory bodies
Luxembourg / Euro — use of national denomination or EU currency denominations in a manner implying State or central-bank affiliation is restricted
Société Anonyme (SA) / S.à r.l. / SECA / SCA / Société Coopérative — misleading legal-form tokens, prohibited for an SCSp unless the entity genuinely adopts that form
Trust / Fiducie / Offshore — misleading or contrary to public policy and transparency standards
Société en Commandite Simple (SCS) — confusingly similar legal-form token, excluded
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its counsel shall: (1) request written reasons from the RCS admission bureau (bureau d'admission) through the LBR/MyGuichet interface; (2) within 15 days from receipt, submit a reasoned re-examination application attaching evidence of prior use, trademark registrations, domain-name ownership, or a notarized statement explaining the distinguishing element; (3) if the re-examination is denied, lodge an administrative appeal before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification, or seek interim relief via référé administratif where imminent harm is shown; (4) alternatively, amend the proposed name with a distinctive prefix, corporate identifier, or registration number and re-submit, which resets the 30-day clearance window without penalty. In practice, the notary will not execute the SCSp deed until a valid negative-confusion certificate is obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. An SCSp engaged in automated global payroll and staff-compliance software must maintain a genuine statutory registered office (siège statutaire) in Luxembourg capable of receiving official process; a licensed registered-agent address satisfies the RCS formality, but for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier and for payroll data processing subject to the GDPR and the Luxembourg Law of 1 August 2018 on data protection, a physical establishment with real administrative substance (payroll compliance staff, HR data controllers, contractual records) is strongly recommended. The appointing notary and the onboarding Luxembourg credit institution may reject a pure virtual mailbox for this industry and risk tier.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — baseline probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is approximately 10% for a service-sector SCSp maintaining commercial substance; the likelihood rises to approximately 35% where the entity operates solely from a virtual mailbox, processes payroll personal data without local GDPR representative substance, or is selected for tax-transparency audit by the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and negative-confusion certificate (certificat de non-confusion) issued by the RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR tariff for electronic filing via MyGuichet

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of formation of the SCSp (acte notarié) including statutory AML/KYC verification of the general partner and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff; prevailing market benchmark EUR 3,500-5,000 for a non-investment-operating SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the partnership agreement (pacte social / contrat de société) and limited-partner subscription documentation by Luxembourg counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Luxembourg law firm (Barreau de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rates (EUR 250-450/hour); flat-fee benchmark EUR 5,000-8,000 for a dual-language deed and LP deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration filing and deposit of constitutive documents with the RCS (Article 15-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of incorporation extracts in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Official Journal (Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial-owner registration with the RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Electronic filing charge via MyGuichet; notary coordination fee included in notarial item

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales); SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016 and codified under Articles 944-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), operating the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic registration declaration (déclaration d'inscription) filed via the LBR/RCS e-filing portal at ejustice.lu
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital and no mandatory escrow account: the SCSp has no minimum paid-up capital requirement; the capital is freely fixed by the partnership agreement, must be fully subscribed, and the contribution schedule is contractually agreed; a notarial deed is required only if immovable property is contributed
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE MANAGER OF [SCSp], dated [Date]. WHEREAS the Partnership Agreement was executed by all initial partners. RESOLVED: (1) the initial unit subscription schedule is approved and acknowledged as fully paid, no escrow being required; (2) the registered office is established at [Address, Luxembourg] for statutory domiciliation; (3) the initial manager is appointed for an indefinite term with sole signature authority; (4) the manager is authorized to file the incorporation dossier with the Luxembourg Business Registers, to publish in the RESA, and to complete tax, VAT, social security and beneficial-owner registrations; (5) all prior actions of the manager are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding partners acting in a private deed, or a Luxembourg notary if immovable property is contributed; optional advice by a Luxembourg corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (convention de société) containing the corporate name, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, capital contribution schedule, profit-sharing ratio, management clause and general partner powers; execute the deed either as a private deed with certified signatures or as a notarial deed; record the contribution schedule and ensure that any agreed capital is actually paid into the partnership bank account prior to RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Capital subscription schedule and contribution payment proof
Identity documents of all initial partners
Declaration of acceptance of the manager (gérant)
Power of attorney if a filing agent is mandated
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any deficiency in the draft deed, re-execute signatures, or convert the private deed into a notarial act if the registrar challenges its authenticity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, via the ejustice.lu/Guichet.lu filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Authenticate on the LBR e-filing platform using a LuxTrust certificate or Luxembourg eID; complete the prescribed electronic insertion form; upload the scanned counterpart of the partnership agreement, the manager's signed acceptance, proof of registered-office address, and the consent of the domiciliation agent; pay the online registration fee; verify the automatic transmission of the dossier to the competent RCS section of the District Court of Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the executed partnership agreement
Proof of registered office (lease contract or domiciliation consent)
Online payment receipt of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a notice of deficiency (régularisation), respond within the two-month statutory window by uploading corrected documents or a supplementary statement; resubmit the corrected e-form if the initial application is closed without registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory publication in the RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RESA publication department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS registration is effective, the registry automatically transmits the mandatory legal mentions to the RESA; the publication is issued electronically, containing the entity name, legal form (SCSp), registered office, corporate purpose, manager identity and duration of the partnership; download the official publication proof and retain it for tax, banking, and client-due-diligence files.
required_dossiers: Extract of the partnership agreement as registered
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Petition the LBR/RCS for a corrective publication if any mandatory mention is missing or erroneous; the registry ordinarily corrects clerical errors ex officio without a court procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and VAT registration with the Luxembourg Inland Revenue and VAT authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); eFiling via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the taxpayer identification number through the ACD/eFiling portal; since the SCSp is tax-transparent, income is attributed to the partners, but the entity must register for formalities if it owes withholding tax on Luxembourg-source fees or salaries or if it invoices VAT; apply for a Luxembourg VAT number via the reverse-charge form/Form 105 where the payroll SaaS platform issues taxable supplies to EU customers; register for net wealth tax at partner level as applicable.
required_dossiers: VAT registration form if taxable activity exists
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contact the ACD competent desk or the AEDT helpline if the taxpayer file remains incomplete; file a spontaneous regularisation of late VAT registration to mitigate any penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), operated by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial-owner declaration within 30 days of incorporation through the LBR/RBE portal; identify every natural person who ultimately owns or controls the SCSp (partners holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of the units, or the general partner controlling the entity); upload the scanned identity documents and an ownership-structure chart; keep the RBE registration receipt in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Identity card or passport of each beneficial owner
Ownership/shareholding diagram showing ultimate natural persons
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing is criminally sanctionable; file immediately upon discovery and rely on the spontaneous-regularisation provisions to reduce any fine; legal counsel may submit a legal memo supporting the ultimate-beneficiary analysis.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration and social security affiliation (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) via the SSIS e-space
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer as soon as the first employee is engaged (including cross-border payroll staff routed through the platform); declare the company in the SSIS portal, obtain the employer registration number, and authenticate the payroll declaration workflow; configure the Direct Debit/ACH and SWIFT rails for social contributions and net salary disbursements; execute the payroll mandate for clients only after the employer number has been issued.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contact the CCSS employer service desk to regularise a late affiliation; pay any late contribution surcharges within 30 days to avoid enforcement action by the social-security recovery office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment permit verification for ISIC 6201 software services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction de l'industrie; online simulator at Guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run the Guichet.lu business-establishment simulator to confirm that automated payroll and staff-compliance software is a purely intellectual IT service outside the regulated trades list; if no permit (autorisation d'établissement) is triggered, the SCSp may commence operations immediately after RCS and tax registration; where prudent, obtain a written non-objection confirmation from the Ministry of the Economy documenting the exclusion from the regulated-professions regime.
required_dossiers: Commercial activity description aligned with NAICS 541214 / ISIC 6201
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authority reclassifies the activity as regulated, file the formal establishment-permit application with professional-good-conduct certificates and a business plan within the applicable deadline, and suspend provisional operation until the permit is granted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Industry and Business Environment Directorate (Ministère de l'Économie)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) – statutorily not required for ISIC 6201 payroll-software services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category D under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; the software activity has negligible environmental footprint
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable: zero process wastewater discharge, no point-source VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste generation; the SCSp must nonetheless comply with general office municipal-waste separation rules, the Law of 27 October 2003 on water management (no contamination), and WEEE obligations for any IT hardware that is placed on the market or decommissioned.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Communal fire-safety certification (certificat de sécurité incendie) for the registered-office premises; structural load inspection certificate from the lessor's engineer for the leased space; workplace occupational-safety clearance under the Labor Code (Code du travail), including the mandatory annual risk assessment (analyse des risques, Article L.312-2) and first-aid/fire drill arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Inland Revenue for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT. Central electronic portal: https://guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in Luxembourg but carrying out taxable activities must appoint a fiscal agent or Luxembourg VAT representative if required. For a payroll SaaS platform with no Luxembourg fixed establishment, VAT registration can be made directly to the AEDT using the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for intra-EU supplies to consumer recipients; a Luxembourg national identification number (matricule) is obtained from the ACD once the entity has a Luxembourg presence for tax filing or payroll reporting; the statutory corporate income tax registration is triggered only upon having a taxable permanent establishment (PE). In practice, obtain a Luxembourg business registration number through the Registry of Commerce (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu, then request a VAT number from the AEDT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory default under Luxembourg law, treated as a pure pass-through for corporate income tax and net wealth tax. No 'check-the-box' election exists as in the US. An SCSp may nonetheless be treated as taxable in another jurisdiction if hybrid mismatch rules apply; Luxembourg has transposed ATAD anti-hybrid rules that can reclassify a transparent entity for Luxembourg tax purposes when payments trigger double-non-taxation or double-deduction outcomes, subject to a Luxembourg effective-tax-residency or place-of-effective-management analysis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA), in accordance with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for Luxembourg-established businesses. Non-resident suppliers of digital services (B2C and B2B without local PE) are required to register from the first euro; alternatively use the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for EUR 10,000 or less in cross-border distance sales into Luxembourg. No VAT registration threshold applies to non-established e-commerce suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: From 1 January 2025, Luxembourg mandates structured electronic invoicing (Peppol-compatible formats) for all domestic B2B transactions between Luxembourg taxable persons. No tax authority pre-clearance or real-time fiscal stalping exists; invoices must be exchanged through certified access points or interoperable Peppol networks. B2G invoices already require PEPPOL. No government API stamping requirement is currently in force, but the AEDT utilises e-audit and tax reporting frameworks to verify VAT compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods removed from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT provided export formalities are completed and transport evidence is held. Services supplied to a non-resident customer (B2B outside the EU) are outside Luxembourg VAT scope, equivalent to zero-rating, where the place of supply is outside the EU. For offshore payroll SaaS services to non-EU business customers, the supply is zero-rated/outside scope upon documentation of the customer's non-EU establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Union manifest / customs approved EEA export declaration)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank evidence of payment received in Luxembourg)
Proof of recipient's non-EU establishment (e.g., VAT registration certificate, company registry extract)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT can conduct retrospective VAT audits for up to five years (ten years in case of fraud). If zero-rating is claimed without adequate documentary proof of export or non-EU place of supply, the AEDT may issue an assessment for the unpaid VAT, plus monthly interest of 0.9% and penalties up to EUR 25,000 per invoice; intentional fraud can lead to criminal fines and imprisonment of up to five years. Non-established taxpayers may be asked to provide financial guarantees. The clawback will include VAT previously zero-rated where physical export or inbound payment evidence does not match the customs declaration within the deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Luxembourg (Banque centrale du Luxembourg, BCL) and the European Central Bank (ECB) as monetary authority for euro-area policy; financial-sector prudential supervision is delegated to the Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current and capital account convertibility under Article 63 TFEU; the euro is a reserve currency with no exchange controls applicable to Luxembourg SCSp treasury operations. Profit remittance and capital distributions to partners are free from any Luxembourg foreign-exchange authorization, subject only to standard AML/KYC documentation, EU sanctions compliance, and tax-transparent reporting rules applicable to the SCSp. Non-resident partners' distributive shares are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax under the pass-through regime absent a Luxembourg commercial establishment or PE, though treaty-based reduced rates may apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline applies to export receipts in Luxembourg or the euro area. Receipts in any currency may be retained in full, transferred at the commercial exchange rate, or used directly for cross-border payables without mandatory conversion to EUR. For the payroll SaaS platform, invoicing of cross-border clients is treated as an EU services export and is not subject to any FX remittance or surrender obligation under BCL regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse de l'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High as an ancillary payment/FX routing tool, but legally unsuitable as the sole or primary treasury vessel. Luxembourg-licensed or EU-authorised e-money institutions (EMIs) such as Wirecard successors, Payoneer, Wise, or Revolut Business can provide multi-currency IBAN accounts, onward SWIFT/SEPA transfer, and competitive FX, but they cannot hold client funds as deposits, provide capital-guaranteed escrow accounts, or act as settlement banks under CSSF rules. For all corporate treasury, payroll clearing, and inbound capital escrow, a fully regulated credit institution with a Luxembourg or EU passport is mandatory; EMIs may not support statutory capital contributions or partner capital accounts in a legally clear manner.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the general partner (gérant or associé-gérant) and all natural-person UBOs at account opening. Remote video KYC is increasingly tolerated in Luxembourg for straightforward structures, but the non-transparent and contract-based SCSp, combined with the payroll platform's medium-risk profile, will normally trigger an in-person interview at at least one banking institution or a remotely notarised power of attorney with legalised corporate package. The bank requires the SCSp deed of partnership, RCS registration extract, UBO register attestation, proof of economic substance at the Luxembourg office, and a list of the general partners and their mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore / opaque ownership chain involving multiple partnership layers and non-EU UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate organigram, chain-of-title chart, UBO register extract, certified partnership agreement, passport and proof-of-address documents for every UBO, legal opinion from a Luxembourg notary confirming the SCSp's existence under LSC 208-1 et seq., and source-of-wealth statement for each participant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp lacks separate legal personality, causing bank account opening and signatory ambiguity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed deed of partnership, notarised powers for the general partner, formal mandate letter, corresponding RCS extract showing the appointed gérant, a Luxembourg counsel legal opinion confirming the authority to open accounts and bind the partnership, and a specimen signature/power-of-attorney attested by a notary or authorised officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payroll software commissions are perceived as potential sanctions-risk or market-abuse transaction flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or internally reviewed financial statements, detailed client invoice register and settlement reports, a business model narrative with the payroll-automation value chain, contract templates with sub-processors, sanctions screening reports for all currencies/countries, and an AML compliance manual aligned with CSSF risk-industry guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Excessive personal wealth opacity or UBO 'borrowing' of capital for SCSp funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds report with bank reference letters, tax residency certificates, dividend/licence agreements, valuation reports, and a police or derogation-free criminal record check for material UBOs or a negative-screening press-search statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative news matrix from publicly accessible PEP or adverse-media databases concerning the partners or the software business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reputational due-diligence report prepared by an external screening provider, written PEP declaration from UBOs, for each adverse hit a narrative explanation and accompanying official court/clarification documents, and a compliance undertaking to bank to report any material change in UBO status or ownership within the contractual 14-day period.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For non-resident equity or capital contributions into the SCSp, the preferred rail is SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) from the investor's bank to the Luxembourg SCSp operational account, accompanied by a purpose reference 'SCSp capital contribution under LSC Art. 208-1' and the SCSp RCS number. For intra-EU inflows, use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with the SCSp's IBAN and a clear code 'CAP_CONTRIBUTION'. BCL statistical balance-of-payments reporting thresholds may require the resident entity to declare the direct investment/capital-account transaction to BCL under the BCL Direct Investment Reporting regime; the underlying purpose code should reflect 'Direct investment — equity capital (D.2/D.3)' as appropriate. The bank must verify the economic substance of the payment by collecting the underlying capital-account entry and the partner resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payroll settlements and software-related disbursements within SEPA, use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst). For non-EU counterparties, use SWIFT MT103 / MT202 COV with correct commercial purpose codes. For higher-value or contractual payroll infrastructure purchases, use a documentary letter of credit confirmed by the Luxembourg bank (SWIFT MT700/MT710) under UCP600, or a standby LC (MT760) for performance/prepayment guarantees. The platform may also connect to direct debit ACH-like schemes within SEPA under SDD Core/B2B for recurring payroll deductions from European employer-managed accounts; all payroll remittances must be segregated from corporate treasury positions to avoid mixing funds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign exchange forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP) with a licensed Luxembourg or EU bank under ISDA or standard FX master agreement
Nondeliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or low-deliverability currencies (e.g. CNY, NGN, GHS, KRW) where only a notional settlement is executed in EUR/USD
Cross-currency interest rate swaps to hedge multi-currency liquidity in debt-instrument or partner-loan structures
European-style FX options (call/put structures) for transactional hedging of upcoming payroll disbursements
FX spot transactions through a regulated counterparty, subject to internal treasury policy and BCL/EU EMIR reporting where applicable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RBE annual confirmation of beneficial owners (annual UBO return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following each anniversary of the SCSp's initial RBE registration; renewal of the confirmation is required at least once per calendar year thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 300 to EUR 2,000 per violation, increased up to EUR 25,000 for legal entities; criminal penalties, including imprisonment, apply for intentional false beneficial-ownership declarations; repeated default blocks issuance of clean RCS/LBR extracts required for banking, notarial, and transactional purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts, general partner's report, and statutory auditor's report — publication in the RCS (obligatory only if the SCSp is a publication-in-scope enterprise; otherwise voluntary filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end (calendar-year filers: on or before 31 July of the following year); publication in the RCS follows within one month after filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish where the obligation applies triggers judicial enforcement by the RCS, injunctions issued by the Tribunal d'arrondissement, and escalating fines up to approximately EUR 10,000; persistent default may expose the general partner to procedural strike-off measures in respect of the SCSp's RCS registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage declaration for social security (annual payroll compliance return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of the year following the payroll reference year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers CCSS administrative fines of up to EUR 1,000 per declaration period, recalculation of social contributions with statutory late-payment interest, and potential payroll attachment or enforcement proceedings for repeated non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The SCSp is not automatically subject to statutory audit. A compulsory independent audit is triggered only when the partnership qualifies under the 'large enterprise' regime of the amended Luxembourg Law of 19 December 2002 — exceeding at least two of three thresholds (total assets above EUR 4.4m; net turnover above EUR 8.8m; average headcount above 50) for two consecutive financial years — or where a CSSF-regulated activity (e.g., fund, payment-services, or financial-sector scope) imposes auditor appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (plan comptable normalisé and the Law of 19 December 2002) is the default accounting framework; IFRS as endorsed by the European Union is permissible for consolidated or voluntary filings; the transparent SCSp records partner capital, profit-sharing allocations, and partner current accounts in its financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner, or its authorised administrator, must keep the RBE file current and confirm its accuracy annually within one month after the anniversary of the SCSp's RBE registration. Any transfer of partnership interests resulting in a change of beneficial ownership — direct or indirect legal or economic ownership of 25% or more of capital, voting rights, or control by other means — must be filed with the RBE within 30 days of the change. Identification documentation for each ultimate beneficial owner must be obtained, verified, and archived under the Luxembourg AML/CFT legal framework.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des Associés) recording capital contributions, profit shares, and all transfers of partnership interests
Register of General Partner and Managing Partners (gérants) with appointment and revocation records
Minute Book / Resolutions Book containing meeting records, written consent resolutions, and capital decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 4,900 per annum for standard Luxembourg registered-office and corporate secretarial agent services (market range EUR 1,200 – EUR 4,500)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 – USD 25,000 per annum for a certified audit of a commercial SCSp operating an automated payroll and HR SaaS platform (market range EUR 7,000 – EUR 23,000); materially lower for a dormant or non-commercial holding SCSp.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 16.80% aggregate Luxembourg CIT headline rate (15% base corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on the base tax + 5% unemployment fund contribution on the base tax). The SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg tax purposes: no entity-level CIT is assessed on the partnership itself; partners are individually taxed on their allocable profit shares.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Zero CIT at the SCSp entity level due to pass-through classification; Luxembourg participation exemption of 100% on qualifying dividends and gains where the corporate partner holds at least a 10% participation for a continuous 12-month period; IP Box regime exempting 80% of qualifying payroll-software IP-derived income; investment tax credit of up to 13% for qualifying digital infrastructure; notional interest deduction on new cash equity.
